original_question: Classify the pairs (C, G) in which C is a nonsingular projective curve of genus at least 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, G is a p-subgroup of Aut(C), and the Nakajima condition (N) holds: g_C > 0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p - 1).
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in the section "p-groups as automorphism groups of curves in characteristic p"—the Lehr–Matignon "big action" classification problem for pairs (C,G) satisfying condition (N)—read together with Proposition 1.2 for the structural consequences of (N), and contrasted with the partial classification proved in Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right geometric objects (a nonsingular projective curve C over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and a p-subgroup G of Aut(C)), and it correctly centers the paper's key largeness hypothesis, namely condition (N): |G|/g_C > 2p/(p-1). It also correctly frames the problem as a classification question for such pairs.
missing_details: The paper works over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0, and G is a finite p-subgroup of Aut_k(C), i.e. of k-automorphisms of C.
The official formulation of condition (N) uses positive genus g_C>0; your draft strengthens this to genus at least 2. That is close in spirit, but it is not literally the paper's hypothesis.

Proposition 1.2 supplies important hidden consequences of (N) that make the question paper-faithful and stand-alone: the quotient C/G is the projective line, the cover C -> C/G has a unique ramification point, and C has p-rank 0.

If the intended target were the proved special case rather than the conjectural classification, then one must add the extra numerical hypothesis |G|/g_C^2 >= 4/(p-1)^2 (equivalently |G| >= 4 g_C^2/(p-1)^2).
Theorem 1.3 does not solve the full classification under (N) alone; it gives an explicit Artin-Schreier-type description only in that stronger range. Your draft does not mention this distinction.
The paper's nearby discussion treats the problem as classifying the resulting 'big' p-group actions after reducing via Proposition 1.2 to the unique wildly ramified point over C/G ≅ P^1.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let C/k be a connected nonsingular projective curve of positive genus, and let G be a finite p-subgroup of Aut_k(C). Assume that (C,G) satisfies condition (N), namely g(C)>0 and |G|/g(C) > 2p/(p-1). By Proposition 1.2 this forces C/G ≅ P^1_k, the cover C -> C/G to have a unique ramification point, and C to have p-rank 0. Classify all such pairs (C,G).
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's main open classification problem in this section, namely Conjecture 1.1, because it uses exactly the largeness hypothesis (N) that the paper singles out on page 153. However, the paper immediately sharpens that setup in Proposition 1.2 (same section, same page) by deriving the geometric reductions that are essential to the intended problem: quotient P^1, unique ramification point, and p-rank 0. Theorem 1.3 on the next page is only a partial answer, obtained after adding the stronger bound |G|/g(C)^2 >= 4/(p-1)^2; therefore your draft is closer to Conjecture 1.1 than to Theorem 1.3, but it needed those hidden reductions to become fully stand-alone and paper-faithful.
